headline: Aerobic efficiency is locked in and back-to-back durability is proven. With St. Olavsleden two weeks out, the taper window has arrived — and loaded, sustained-climb specificity never entered the picture.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The recent four-week block landed a substantial volume jump while holding easy-run HR in its lower band, which is exactly what you want going into a multi-day self-supported effort — the durability base is real, not borrowed. Strength has stayed frequent through the same window, sitting almost entirely in low zones, so it's supporting the running rather than competing with it. Steps remain very high even on rest days, meaning your true daily load is higher than the run log alone suggests, and that background time-on-feet matters more than usual for what's coming. The one genuine gap remains terrain: none of this volume carried a loaded pack or sustained climbing, so the crossing's specific demand is still untested. Recovery signals are mixed and the cardio-load status reads as detraining, which almost certainly reflects a real recent drop in logged running — appropriate this close to the start, not a concern.
sections.trends: The 16-week shape is clearly a build-then-consolidate rhythm rather than a flat plateau, and the year-to-date jump against the same point last year is enormous — you're operating in a completely different volume tier than a year ago. That trajectory makes sense for someone building durable year-round hybrid capacity, and the recent block's expansion followed by an easing edge fits a deliberate approach to the event window rather than any loss of momentum.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace remains sharp from the early-July measurement, and there's no signal it's eroded — the easy work has been protecting aerobic fitness, not blunting it. But with insufficient rolling baseline history, treat the single figure as a reference point rather than a trend. For the crossing, threshold speed isn't the limiter anyway; sustained low-intensity economy over days is, and that's the quality your recent runs actually demonstrate.
sections.zones: The distribution is strongly aerobic, which is right for this phase — the long runs and easy sessions sit predominantly in Z1–Z2 with only brief excursions higher. The per-session shapes confirm it: your recent long and mid-distance runs are genuinely steady, not disguised interval sessions, with only the earlier faster session carrying meaningful Z3 time. That's the appropriate texture heading into a self-supported multi-day effort where control, not intensity, is the skill being rehearsed.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions continue to sit low and steady, confirming these are functional/conditioning-flavoured rather than maximal-load days — sensible alongside the running volume. The two most recent strength sessions carry no HR at all, so there's less to read there, but nothing in the pattern suggests strength work is adding hidden cardiovascular strain. Sensor sources agree well enough across runs that effort judgements hold regardless of origin.
sections.calendar: The mix of running and strength across the block shows a well-distributed week rather than clustering, and the back-to-back-capable spacing has quietly built the multi-day tolerance the crossing needs. The strength cadence has held its own rhythm alongside running without either crowding the other — a sign the schedule is genuinely sustainable rather than propped up by good weeks.
sections.personal_bests: Your standing 5K through Half bests were all set in a faster-focused window last year, and current training is deliberately pointed elsewhere — endurance economy, not top-end speed — so none are realistic targets in this window, nor should they be. The relevant "best" right now is durability over consecutive days, which won't show on the PB board but is exactly what you're sharpening.

watch_items: Watch whether any loaded-pack or elevation-heavy session appears before the start — still the single open variable, and the last realistic window to touch it is closing.
Watch how easy-run HR behaves as logged volume drops into the taper; a continued low band confirms freshness rather than lost stimulus.
Watch that the taper doesn't over-shed — the goal is arriving fresh, not detrained, so some quality time-on-feet should remain.
Keep a loose eye on recovery consistency as pre-event logistics build; erratic patterns are worth noting but not overreacting to this close in.
